newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, U.S. to hold more aviation talks.
newsitem.headline: Japan, U.S. to hold more aviation talks.

text.p: Japan and the United States agreed on Saturday to resume talks in Washington on a dispute over aircraft landing rights, a senior Japanese Transport Ministry official said on Saturday.
The official, who spoke on condition he not be identified, said that no date had been set but that the talks could resume in February.
He also said that the the atmosphere in exploratory talks in Tokyo on Friday and Saturday had improved from previous discussions.
"It's quite different from previous negotiations. We had quite frank discussions," he told reporters.
Ending the "exploratory" talks, the two countries earlier confirmed that they could not accept each other's proposals.
The United States wants Japan to adopt an "open skies" policy aimed at lifting all government restrictions on airline services except for safety and security rules.
But Japan believes "open skies" would lead to the domination of international markets by U.S. airlines and has called on Washington to open its domestic market first.
Formal discussions between the two nations on the long-running dispute broke down in August.
